item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's not downright bad but I do have one big problem with this, and it's a simple one… it's not an SCP.

No seriously, what about it is abnormal? We know it's a parasitic worm (which exist in real life so nothing unusual about that), its behaviour, biology, feeding method and mating habits are well documented and understood. The only kind of weird thing about it is its reaction to stimuli, and even then there is nothing extraordinary about it.

There is nothing about it that can't be rationally explained. It's just a previously unknown species of parasitic worm. I wouldn't be surprised if there were real species we don't understand as well as this thing. It's not an SCP. It's not even anomalous. In fact, the Foundation is actively making things worse by hiding its existence from the public, thus preventing them from protecting themselves from it.

I'm also kind of confused by the containment procedures. The way it's written, it seems to imply that this things is deadly, with procedures given to dispose of bodies and euthanasia of infected animals being mandatory, yet nothing in the description indicates that this worm is more than a mild inconvenience, if even that.

And finally…

Mature eggs can remain viable for up to █ years after the death of their parent

Am I the only one who gets really annoyed by the seemingly random masking of numbers like this? Why would it be important to hide it? How is public knowledge of that number a threat to the Foundation's work? And it's especially pointless in this case since only one number is masked, so we know by default that this time is anywhere between 2 and 9 years.

It's far from the only article to do this and I just don't get it. It seems like a pointless convention that people repeat simply because they've seen other people do it, without wondering if there's actually a point to it.

item.title: Why is this an SCP, though?
item.content:encoded:
This is exactly what I was wondering, Matt, and it's part of the reason I signed up for a Wikidot account. First off, I do LIKE this SCP. I also think it needs an "added something" for it to actually BE an SCP, though.

If it's not particularly dangerous, with no suspected "supernatural" origins and nothing any more creepy than a lot of other parasites then why does it need to be kept secret/SCP? It seems like a waste of resources. I have seen fistfuls of 4+-inch roundworms fall out of a live dog and proceed to wrap themselves tightly around nearby carpet, and there's fungus out there that controls insect movement. This doesn't seem much different/worse. I know not all SCPs have to be dangerous, alien etc, but there should be some kind of minimum requirement, and this doesn't feel like it reaches that.

It's a creepy idea but it feels to me like something needs to be added for it to be an actual SCP.
